clue.text: Foxy lady's top in reflected light, invisible before long

indicators.note: the reversed letters come before the next piece in the answer
a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters of this pair are read backwards

parts.note: ultraviolet light is invisible to the eye, abbreviated UV

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, here taken from the word lady's

parts.note: to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: A cunning woman's top glimpsed in a mirror, unseen before she longs for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns L plus UV (the lady's top letter with ultraviolet) into VUL; 'in' just places the L with the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulpine is the adjective for foxes, so it means foxy or sly in character.

clue.text: Size of knob

definitions.meaning: the amount of space something takes up, its capacity
the dial on a radio or amplifier that sets how loud it is

explanation.surface: Asking how big a door handle is.
explanation.definitionFit: Volume means size or capacity, and a volume control is a familiar knob on any audio set.

clue.text: Like a wolf bearing a flower on top

indicators.note: in a down light the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: the lupin is a tall garden flower with spikes of pea-like blooms
a compass bearing such as E, for east

explanation.surface: A wolf wearing a flower on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupine is the adjective from Latin lupus, wolf, so it describes anything wolflike.

clue.text: Agent and compiler's for acquiring eastern garb

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, so compiler's is I'm, written IM

indicators.note: the word for takes in the other pieces, holding them inside it

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a sari is the draped garment worn by women in South Asia

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be an agent who favours oriental dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiler's' is the setter saying 'I am'; 'acquiring' wraps PRO around the eastern garment and its E.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario is a theatrical manager or promoter, someone acting as an agent for performers.

clue.text: More old paintings put up

parts.note: ex means former, so old

indicators.note: in a down light, put up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: More of the old pictures get hung on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ART into TRA in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, so it can stand in for more in a sentence like 'at no more cost'.

clue.text: Seduced compiler to be indecent, somehow

indicators.note: the letter for the setter sits inside the shuffled letters
somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The setter was lured into behaving rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indecent' splits as 'in' plus 'decent': 'somehow' rearranges DECENT to ENTCED, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enticed is to be tempted or lured, the same sense as being seduced.

clue.text: Raise it with signal about playground trees

indicators.note: about here means jumbled around, an order changed

parts.note: a cue is a signal to begin
a play area, PLAY

indicators.note: in a down light, raising a word writes it upwards, bottom to top

explanation.surface: An instruction to lift something with a signal near a children's play area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CUE plus PLAY to EUCALYP; 'Raise' turns IT to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypti is a plural of eucalyptus, the gum trees of Australia.

clue.text: Regularly strip — topless any minute

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word strip
the word any loses its top, which in a down light is its first letter

explanation.surface: A striptease where someone may go topless at any moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of strip, TI; 'topless' cuts A from any to leave NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, said 'my-newt', means extremely small, a synonym of tiny.

clue.text: "Entrée de Chanel 20", as they might say in Paris

indicators.text: as they might say in Paris
indicators.note: a French speaker's pronunciation is being imitated, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: the designer Coco Chanel supplies Coco, and twenty in French is vingt

explanation.surface: It looks like a French perfume name, in the style of Chanel No 5.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in French, 'Coco vingt' comes out close to the name of the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Coq au vin, chicken braised in red wine, is a classic French main course or entrée.

clue.text: More forlorn, darling? That's right — that's about right

indicators.note: the second that's refers to the whole build so far, which goes about, or around, another letter

parts.note: dear is a term of endearment, like darling
R again for right
that's is that is, Latin id est, abbreviated IE
R again for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks if their sweetheart is more miserable and gets a weary confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'that's' means the whole build so far; 'that's about' wraps it around one more R, giving the middle R.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, gloomy and sad, so its comparative means more forlorn.

clue.text: Relish looking back at an early stage

indicators.note: looking back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: pupal describes the pupa, an insect's early stage of development

explanation.surface: Enjoying a look back at the early days of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up is to accept eagerly or enjoy, as in relishing praise.

clue.text: A university dropout to teach unique method

indicators.note: dropout says the letters are dropped out of the jumbled phrase

explanation.surface: A student who left university now teaches an unusual way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: TEACH UNIQUE holds every letter of the answer plus A and U; 'dropout' takes those two away and the rest are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique is a particular way of carrying out a task, a synonym of method.

clue.text: Low bridges across central development in the city

indicators.note: the word goes either side of the other letters, spanning them

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make

indicators.note: development means the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Low bridges spanning a city-centre building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the verb for what cattle do, not 'not high'; 'development' shuffles the middle word and 'bridges across' splits the moo around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Carlo is the city in Monaco famed for its casino.

clue.text: Sound content to reverse some of the corruption

indicators.note: the letters taken are then read from right to left
only some of the word's letters are used, a run from inside it

explanation.surface: A plea to undo part of a system's corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' takes RRUP from corruption and 'to reverse' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat makes a low rumbling noise when contented, so this is the sound of contentment.

clue.text: Wears feathers and leaves the witness box

parts.note: to wear something in the sense of tolerate it is to stand it
down is the soft fine plumage of birds

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in plumage gets up and leaves court.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness stands down when they finish giving evidence and step out of the box.

clue.text: Hawkish marine, left motherless after accident, has another depression

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer
one dip in the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a pit is a hollow, another kind of depression besides a dent

indicators.note: the word marine is left without MA, the familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An aggressive soldier, orphaned in an accident, falls into a second depression.
explanation.walkthrough: In accident, the dent (one depression) is swapped for PIT (another), giving ACCIPIT; marine without MA gives RINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Accipitrine means relating to hawks, from the Latin accipiter, a hawk.

clue.text: Elect representation to enshrine a legal right for customers

indicators.note: to enshrine is to enclose something as if in a shrine, so it holds the other piece
a representation presents the letters in a new arrangement

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Elected representatives should enshrine a legal right for consumers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elect representation' reads like politics, but 'representation' just shuffles the word, and 'to enshrine' puts the lien in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of clients or customers of a shop or business.

clue.text: Grandmother having fun at 99

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
a jest is a joke, fun
IC is one less than C, 100, a crossword-only way to write 99 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An old lady enjoying herself at the age of 99.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grandmother' splits into 'Grand' and 'mother'. Strictly 99 is XCIX in Roman numerals; IC is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means stately and imposing, much the same as grand.

clue.text: Hooked with 24 resulting in equalisation

indicators.note: the answer and the other piece together result in the word equalisation when their letters are mixed

parts.note: the answer to clue 24, a colonnade of ancient Greece

explanation.surface: A sporting tale of a goal from a hook shot that levels the score.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus STOA, the solution to 24, can be rearranged into EQUALISATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquiline means like an eagle, and is used of a nose that is curved or hooked like a beak.

clue.text: Getting clear one that's charged is to be held inside

indicators.note: the little word is to be held inside the other piece

parts.note: to acquit is to clear someone of a charge
an ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Someone charged in court is to be detained despite being cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' and 'charged' look like court words; only the first is, and the second is the physics sense. 'to be held inside' puts the 'is' in the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquisition is the act of getting or obtaining something.

clue.text: Mousy brown hair you see Armani team finally modelled

indicators.note: modelled means shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
finally points to the last letter of each word in turn

explanation.surface: A fashion show where a model with brown hair walks for the Armani team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes N, R, U, E, I, M, and 'modelled' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Murine is the zoological adjective for mice and rats, so it means mouselike.

clue.text: Externally, woman — internally, very furious dragon

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first
externally takes only the outside letters of the word woman
furious means wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A woman who seems calm outside but is seething within is a dragon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Externally' keeps only the outer letters of woman; 'furious' shuffles very, and 'internally' sets that between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a winged two-legged dragon of heraldry.

clue.text: Like the villain of the piece (and the other way round)

definitions.text: Like the villain of the piece

indicators.note: read with its words the other way round, the phrase becomes piece of the villain, telling us to take a part of those words
this says the phrase before it also works in reverse word order, as an instruction for a hidden run

explanation.surface: Describing the bad guy of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the clue defines; read 'the other way round' it becomes 'piece of the villain', and a piece of 'the villain' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The villain of a play is the wicked character, and wicked is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Actor is subject to scrutiny

parts.note: under means subject to, as in under orders
close study is scrutiny

explanation.surface: A performer is being closely examined.
explanation.definitionFit: An understudy is an actor who learns another's part to stand in if needed.

clue.text: The principle of sauce thickening

indicators.note: of says the letters come from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cook explains the basic rule for making a sauce thicker.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of sauce into the start of thickening.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle guiding behaviour.

clue.text: St Thomas regularly seen in a place of philosophical discourse

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, starting with the first, across both words

explanation.surface: Saint Thomas Aquinas often appears in a seat of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a Greek portico; Zeno taught in one, which gave the Stoic school its name.

clue.text: The IRA tied the ends off at the end of the month

indicators.note: the end letter of each of the four words is cut off

explanation.surface: Terrorists tied up loose ends before the month was out.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last letter of The, IRA, tied and the leaves TH, IR, TIE, TH.
explanation.definitionFit: In a thirty-day month, the thirtieth day is the last one.

clue.text: Sheepish one to accept tiny position?

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the word one holds the other piece

parts.note: taken as the word itself
the clue for TINY is in position 6 down in this grid, six being VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone feeling embarrassed about taking a lowly job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiny position' points to the grid number of 6-down, whose answer is TINY: 6 is VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means relating to sheep, so it is literally sheepish.

clue.text: The alternative to bury compiler back in box

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The setter is put back in a box rather than buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME into EM, which goes into CRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cremate a body, burning it to ashes, is the usual alternative to burial.

clue.text: Is youngster able to eat here?

parts.note: can means is able to
a teen is a teenager, a youngster

explanation.surface: Asking whether a child is able to eat at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, 'Is youngster able to' becomes 'can teen'; the setter's question mark marks the definition as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria at a school, factory or barracks, a place where people eat.
